issues.body:
The new block gates only on `patterns.len() >= 3 && crate::dp::active().is_some()`, after `plan` has already been resolved to "binary GOO" or "worst-case-optimal (LFTJ)" — it does not gate on `bgp_uses_binary(&patterns)`.

DPccp is reachable only on the binary path: `bgp_uses_binary` is `!(patterns.len() >= 3 && bgp_is_cyclic(patterns))` (exec.rs:6893-6895), `eval_flat_conjunctive` dispatches on it, and the `#[cfg(feature = "dp-planner")] if let Some(cfg) = crate::dp::active()` / `eval_bgp_dp` block lives inside `eval_bgp_binary`. A cyclic 3+-pattern BGP takes the LFTJ arm and never calls `dp::plan`.

So on a triangle such as `{ ?a :p ?b . ?b :q ?c . ?c :r ?a }` the default-build server prints:

  BGP [worst-case-optimal (LFTJ)] (3 patterns, 0 filters) [DPccp may execute; displayed tree is a greedy replay, not an execution record]

Both halves are false: DPccp cannot execute that shape, and the rendered order is an LFTJ global variable order, not a greedy join tree.

Secondary imprecision in the same string: `trace_label` also labels the EXPLAIN ANALYZE trace node (via `trace::enter` at exec.rs:4605) and the explain-json operator labels (explain_json.rs:257/:265 via `trace_label_pub`). In the ANALYZE case the node carries measured row counts and wall time — it IS an execution record — so "not an execution record" reads wrong there even on the binary path; only the greedy sub-tree rendering in explain.rs is a replay.

explain.rs is correct by construction because its LFTJ branch returns early at explain.rs:289-313. exec.rs lacks the equivalent guard. This was round 2's minor #1 with the exact fix spelled out; it is unchanged.
issues.fix_hint:
Add the dispatch guard so exec.rs matches explain.rs's scoping:

    if bgp_uses_binary(&patterns) && patterns.len() >= 3 && crate::dp::active().is_some() { ... }

`bgp_uses_binary` is already in scope in this module (exec.rs:6893) and is the exact predicate `eval_flat_conjunctive` dispatches on. Consider also sourcing the `>= 3` literal from dp's own gate (`plan()`'s `(3..=MAX_PATTERNS)`) so the two cannot drift.

Optionally tighten the wording for the ANALYZE context, e.g. "[DPccp may execute; join order shown is a greedy replay]" — dropping "not an execution record", which is inaccurate on a traced node that carries real actuals.
issues.title: Unfixed from round 2: trace_label appends the DPccp note to cyclic (LFTJ) BGPs where DPccp cannot run, and calls the LFTJ order a "greedy replay"

issues.body:
Both new tests (`dp_eligible_text_explain_discloses_greedy_replay`, `dp_eligible_json_explain_discloses_greedy_replay`) assert only that the note is PRESENT on a DP-eligible 3-pattern BGP. `accept_header_requests_explain` asserts the greedy label for the 2-pattern JOIN_QUERY with `contains`, which passes whether or not the note is also emitted.

Consequently nothing goes red when the note is emitted too widely — which is exactly the live failure mode in exec.rs::trace_label described above. The tests are not vacuous (they target the exact new strings and would fail if the note were dropped), but they only cover one direction of the guard.
issues.fix_hint: Add `assert!(!body.contains("DPccp may execute"), "{body}")` for the 2-pattern JOIN_QUERY in `accept_header_requests_explain`, and add a 3-pattern CYCLIC (triangle) BGP case asserting the same absence once the exec.rs guard lands. Both are cheap additions to the existing spawned-server tests and would have caught the exec.rs gap.
issues.title: Unfixed from round 2: no negative test pins the ABSENCE of the DPccp note, so over-disclosure is unguarded

verdict.summary:
Round 3 sees the SAME code as round 2 (HEAD is f6370a32, "repair failing CI legs for #4098 (round 2)"); nothing has landed since. All five round-2 findings persist verbatim at the same severities -> stagnant.

Re-verified as correct: DPccp is order-only on a commutative/associative natural join, so the default-on forwarding is result-equivalent; planning is genuinely bounded (dp.rs count_csg takes an early-abort cap; plan() gates on 3..=63 patterns, max_subgraphs=4096, plus a pair cap of max_subgraphs*128), and the "planning does not poll QueryBudget" residual is disclosed. explain.rs scopes its NOTE correctly by construction (LFTJ returns early at :289-313, so the NOTE at :324 is binary-only). `without_dp_planner` is a real pub export (lib.rs:137) and sparq-core is a direct server dependency, so dp_planner_default.rs is a genuine compile-time forwarding tripwire. The two new explain tests are non-vacuous.

Why request_changes rather than round 2's approve: the one substantive defect is unchanged and is the PR's own stated deliverable. exec.rs::trace_label appends the disclosure without the `bgp_uses_binary` guard explain.rs gets for free, so a triangle BGP (`{?a :p ?b . ?b :q ?c . ?c :r ?a}`) — reachable from any default-build server — prints two false claims: DPccp definitively cannot execute that shape (bgp_uses_binary = !(len>=3 && cyclic) routes it to LFTJ; dp::plan is only called inside eval_bgp_binary), and the shown order is an LFTJ variable order, not a greedy replay. The fix is one conjunct, was written out in round 2's fix_hint, and was not applied. Shipping a known-false string in user-facing EXPLAIN twice running is not something to wave through on a change whose whole purpose is honest disclosure.

Severity deliberately NOT escalated: the note is advisory-only and errs toward over-warning. No blocker/major; the hold is on the unaddressed minor.

No injection content in the diff or the prior-round block.
